clare: Quick RFC follow-up: proposing 'shard-and-fizzle' fallback. Instead of one backup, split a tiny shard of traffic to several fallbacks, then "fizzle" them (decay weights) if quality or cost breaches. Goal: avoid a hard quality cliff and spread tail risk. Thoughts?

neha: Like the risk-spreading idea. Main asks: off-hot-path decision plane, signed weight blobs, and a per-route cost leash.

ross: Ops: need immediate global kill (synchronous), per-variant metrics, and weight-change audit events. Also a small simulator so SREs can dry-run shards.

samir: Algorithm sketch: start with micro-shards (0.5%-2%) across N fallbacks, monitor quality_signal + latency, apply exponential fizzle (half-life) on failing shards, and rehydrate if signals recover. Enforce cost_leash (cents/min) and minimum dwell time to avoid thrash.

clare: Ownership: Platform owns DeploymentSpec.fallback (mode=shard-and-fizzle, variants[], cost_leash, min_dwell_ms). Broker computes signed blobs {route, weights[], gen, ttl, sig} and publishes to pubsub. Routers apply blobs only if gen newer and sig valid. Router also checks emergency_kill flag synchronously.

neha: Sticky-session: add affinity_token window so sessions stick to same shard for M requests to preserve KV warmth. Also expose an effective-weights endpoint for oncall.

ross: Debugging hooks: broker /explain?req_id=... returns rule trace + tiny timeseries. Simulator CLI: `platform tool simulate-shard --route R --profile P` to preview weight evolution.

samir: Also require a quality_signal in telemetry and allow a small callback hook for product teams to plug domain-specific scorers. Keep decision logic out of hot path.
